article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Evening Brief
article.dek: New England loses its top receiver the day before hosting the Raiders, the Cardinals' line takes another hit, and both headline cards point at the Vikings.

items.headline: Patriots lose their leading receiver on Saturday
paragraphs: New England placed wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) on injured reserve Saturday. He leads the Patriots with 15 catches for 209 yards and must miss at least four games. Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) is already on IR, and fullback Reggie Gilliam joined them there.

That leaves Sunday's receiver group against Las Vegas as Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. And that game is the Value card game — Raiders +3.5 at 1:00 p.m. ET Sunday. If your book's number moved on this news, tap Check and run your exact line and price through the evaluator.
items.takeaway: The news lands on the Value card game. Bet the number in front of you, not yesterday's.

items.headline: Cardinals' banged-up line loses another starter
paragraphs: Arizona placed starting right guard Isaiah Adams (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday — the second starting lineman to hit IR, after left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. was ruled out for the season on Oct. 5. Backup Jon Gaines II likely steps in against Detroit on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.
Detroit's defense comes to town averaging 3.8 sacks per game, second-best in the league. That's the matchup, stated plainly.
items.takeaway: A backup right guard against a top pass rush — watch the pregame line on Detroit.

items.headline: Saturday's other game statuses
paragraphs: The Bills ruled out receiver Joshua Palmer (shoulder, hurt in Friday's practice) and defensive tackle Ed Oliver (knee) for Monday night at the Rams; receiver DJ Moore (shoulder), cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) and lineman Landon Jackson (knee) are questionable. Cornerback Christian Benford returns after missing last week.

The Colts listed receiver Keenan Allen (groin), receiver Darius Slayton (knee) and cornerback Charvarius Ward (groin) as questionable against Pittsburgh; Allen and Ward were full participants Friday and are expected to play. Cleveland ruled quarterback Dillon Gabriel out for Sunday.
The rest of Friday's final reports still stand — Hall, Bosa, Darrisaw, Hooker, Dell and the rest are already decided. Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Questionable is not out and out is not questionable — plan around the outs, check the rest at the inactive deadline.

items.headline: Quarterback room: no new changes since this morning
paragraphs: The app's quarterback feed is fresh and nothing moved since the morning board. Tyson Bagent starts for Chicago at Lambeau (announced Monday; Caleb Williams is out with a hamstring). Tyler Huntley is still Baltimore's expected starter for Sunday night at Atlanta — the board has priced Lamar Jackson's absence since Friday.

Kyler Murray starts for Minnesota, Jameis Winston for the Giants, Cam Ward for Tennessee, and Jayden Daniels is expected to play for Washington. The board refreshes every morning and evening — if a Sunday-morning report changes any starter, the app hasn't seen it yet, so check before kickoff.
items.takeaway: No new QB news today. The contingencies are already in the prices.

items.headline: Sunday weather: rain in Washington, Pittsburgh and New Jersey
paragraphs: Final National Weather Service forecasts for the Sunday 1:00 p.m. ET window stand as published this morning: Landover (Giants at Commanders) — rain, about 70°F, near-100% chance. Pittsburgh (Colts at Steelers) — showers and thunderstorms, mid-60s, wind 9 to 13 mph. MetLife (Browns at Jets) — rain, mid-60s, 93% chance.

Miami runs hot (low 90s), Nashville has about a 50-50 shot of rain, Foxborough stays mostly dry in the low 60s, Lambeau is sunny near 80°F, and Seattle is sunny in the low 60s. Weather is information, not an edge — note which games could get sloppy, then price your book's total in Check like always.
items.takeaway: Three 1:00 p.m. ET games look wet. File it, don't force it.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate and Balanced are both on the Vikings tonight
paragraphs: Both headline cards point at the same play: Minnesota moneyline -130 on DraftKings. The model's own number on the Vikings is 69.4% against the market's 56.3%.

Remember what the cards mean. Hit Rate is which supported pick looks most likely to win — it forgoes value for win probability. Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, a good starting point. The app's tutorial says it straight: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
items.takeaway: Same team, two reasons. Hit Rate chases the win; Balanced chases the middle ground.

items.headline: Balanced got re-dealt: Chicago off, Minnesota on
paragraphs: This morning the Balanced card was Chicago moneyline -124. Tonight the model deals Balanced to Minnesota at -130 on DraftKings instead. Cards are re-dealt every refresh — bet the card in front of you, not this morning's.

If your book shows Minnesota at a different price than -130, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet/no-bet verdict on your price — a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: When the card changes, the play changes. Check your book's number.

items.headline: Value is still the model's +EV play: Raiders +3.5
paragraphs: Raiders +3.5 at -105 on FanDuel holds the only plus-expected-value tag on the board. The model gives Las Vegas a 50.6% chance against the market's 48.6% — a small positive edge at MEDIUM reliability.
That is what the Value card means, every single day: the model thinks the price beats fair. +EV is a property of the price, not the team.
items.takeaway: Value is always the +EV card. Tonight it's Raiders +3.5.

items.headline: Closing line value — the price race you can actually win
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine you bet Team X at -110 on Friday. By Sunday the same bet costs -130. You beat the closing number — your price was better than the market's final price. That's closing line value, or CLV.

One win of CLV proves nothing. But bettors who consistently beat the close tend to be finding genuinely good prices, because the closing number is the market's most informed guess. It's the one race against the market where you get a scoreboard before the game even starts.
items.takeaway: You can't control the bounce of the ball, but you can control the price you pay — beating the closing number is the mark of a good process.

items.headline: Vikings get cheaper through the day
paragraphs: Minnesota moneyline drifted cheaper during the day: DraftKings went from -142 this morning to -130 tonight; FanDuel held at -134. Both cards stayed supported and both stayed bets.
-130 means every $1.30 you risk wins $1. A cheaper price on the same card is the market giving you a better number — and the card followed it to DraftKings.
items.takeaway: The price moved, the pick didn't. Shop it.

items.headline: Falcons drift back to -3.0 on DraftKings
paragraphs: Baltimore at Atlanta: DraftKings came back to Atlanta -3.0 (-122) from this morning's -3.5, while FanDuel holds Atlanta -3.5 at even money. Same game, different number.
If your book's number isn't the card's number, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet/no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Your book's line is the only line that matters. Check it.

items.headline: Pittsburgh split stands; Chicago gets two cents pricier
paragraphs: The Steelers-Colts split is unchanged: DraftKings has Pittsburgh -3.0 (-102) while FanDuel shows -2.5 (-115) — that half point is exactly what the hook lesson was about. Chicago moneyline went from -125 to -130 on DraftKings (FanDuel steady at -124) with Bagent starting at Lambeau on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: Half points and stale numbers are where Check earns its keep.

items.headline: Saturday night job: shop tonight's card prices now
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and tonight's cards are dealt: Vikings -130, Raiders +3.5. Pull those two prices from your own book before bed and compare. Anything that doesn't match the card price goes through Check before you touch it on Sunday.
Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff — give the app one more look in the morning in case a scratch moves a number.
items.takeaway: Shop the price before the game, not during it.

items.headline: Two cards, one team — don't double the bet
paragraphs: Hit Rate and Balanced both land on Minnesota tonight. That means the app's two different lenses agree — not that you should bet it twice. The cards describe different reasons (likeliest winner vs. strong pick at a fair price), not different bets.
Size it once, the way the app suggests for your bankroll, and let the single ticket carry both reasons.
items.takeaway: Agreement across cards is a signal, not a second stake.
